producer_report.summary: The read-only host-rules check is in place in crates/athena-core/src/host_rules.rs, registered in lib.rs. It GETs `repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/{branch}` for athena/records and main, using the new `gh::get_args` helper (args are just `["api", path]`). For each branch it reports force-push forbidden, deletion forbidden and up-to-date required as in force, not in force, or unknown. A runner error, unparseable JSON, or a reply that isn't a JSON array makes all three rules on that branch unknown. The report and the module doc both say only rulesets are seen, not classic branch protection. The CHANGELOG entry cites §3 and §10, and records-history.md §10 item 1 is updated. After the send-back I changed no code. I re-ran the gates and the host_rules tests. I could not re-read the saved full-suite output, so I did not confirm its exit status or tail myself.

open_issues: I could not see the tail of the full `cargo test --locked` output, so its exit status is inferred from the absence of an error. Athena's own run will confirm it.
Whether the live rules/branches reply is a plain JSON list at the current API version is assumed from the brief and was not checked against the live host.
mistakes: I did not capture the tail of the full `cargo test --locked` output. It was too large to display, and I cannot read the saved copy.
learnings: The Bash policy hook denies double-quoted expansions such as `$?`, so exit statuses can't be echoed. Success shows as a command that returns with no error.
Large tool output is saved outside the working directory, and Grep and Read cannot reach it.
desires: A way to see the exit status and last lines of long commands, such as `cargo test`, without piping.
